newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK railway projects seen costing HK$50 billion.
newsitem.headline: HK railway projects seen costing HK$50 billion.

text.p: Hong Kong could spend some HK$50 billion by 2001 on developing priority railway projects, Financial Secretary Donald Tsang said on Wednesday.
The government had contributed HK$49 billion for the construction of the territory's airport and airport railway over the past three years, Tsang said in his annual budget speech.
The future govenment may have to contribute a similar sum between 1998 and 2001 toward the construction of the high priority projects under the territory's Railway Development Strategy, he said.
"The several railway projects would cost HK$50 billion as an initial estimate," Tsang later told a news conference.

Treasury Secretary K.C. Kwong told reporters the details of the projects were still in the hands of the territory's two railway firms -- the Mass Transit Railway Corp and the Kowloon-Canton Railway Corp -- and government consultants.
The amount, form and timing of future allocations were yet to be thrashed out and were not included in the government's medium term forecasts, he said.
But agreements with the railway companies could be reached late this year or early next year, allowing for more information to become available, he said.
The proposed railway lines include a new line linking urban areas with the western New Territories district as well as extensions of the subway system.
